presentation.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began insidiously after a house move. She describes a fine tremor that interferes with writing on the board, proximal weakness climbing stairs, loose stools three to four times daily, and oligomenorrhoea for the last two cycles. Her partner has noticed that her eyes look 'startled' and she reports gritty discomfort and retro-orbital pressure, worse on waking. No neck pain, no recent iodinated contrast, no amiodarone, no over-the-counter supplements, and no thyroid hormone in the household.
presentation.social_history: Never smoked (relevant: smoking is the strongest modifiable risk factor for progression of thyroid eye disease). Alcohol 4 units/week. No recreational drug use.

review_of_systems.cardiovascular: Palpitations, exertional dyspnoea, no chest pain, no syncope
review_of_systems.gastrointestinal: Increased stool frequency, no blood, no steatorrhoea
review_of_systems.neuromuscular: Fine tremor, proximal myopathy, anxiety, insomnia
review_of_systems.ophthalmic: Grittiness, lid retraction, no diplopia, no visual loss
review_of_systems.dermatological: Warm moist skin, onycholysis of the fourth fingernail, no pretibial changes

examination_findings: Smooth, symmetrically enlarged goitre approximately 45 g with an audible bruit over both lobes
Bilateral lid retraction and lid lag; proptosis 21 mm right and 22 mm left by Hertel exophthalmometry
Clinical Activity Score 2/7 (retrobulbar discomfort, conjunctival injection); no chemosis, no optic neuropathy
Fine postural tremor of the outstretched hands
Warm, moist palms; sinus tachycardia with a systolic flow murmur
Proximal weakness MRC 4/5 at the hip flexors; brisk reflexes with a fast relaxation phase
No pretibial myxoedema, no thyroid acropachy

lab_panels.comment: Baseline, drawn before any antithyroid drug.

results.interference_note: Oestrogen-containing contraceptive raises thyroxine-binding globulin; total T4 overstates the excess relative to FT4.

lab_panels.analyser: Roche Cobas e801 (ECLIA) / Thermo Fisher Phadia 250
lab_panels.comment: TRAb requested on the same specimen as the baseline TFT.

results.interference_note: Raised, i.e. NOT suppressed: excludes exogenous thyroid hormone as the cause of the thyrotoxicosis.

lab_panels.comment: Mandatory baseline before carbimazole: a later neutropenia cannot be interpreted without it.

results.interference_note: Mild transaminitis is common in untreated thyrotoxicosis itself; it is not a contraindication to carbimazole but must be documented before starting.
Bone isoenzyme; reflects thyrotoxic high bone turnover.

lab_panels.comment: Four weeks on carbimazole 30 mg daily plus propranolol 40 mg three times daily.

results.interference_note: Still suppressed: thyrotroph recovery lags free hormone normalisation by weeks to months. Dose titration at this visit must be driven by FT4 and FT3, not TSH.

lab_panels.comment: Routine four-week check; patient asymptomatic, no sore throat or fever.
Twelve weeks; carbimazole reduced to 15 mg daily, propranolol stopped.
Six months; carbimazole 10 mg daily. Biochemically and clinically euthyroid.

results.interference_note: Falling but still positive at six months; a TRAb that remains positive at the end of an 18-month course predicts relapse and argues for definitive therapy.

imaging.findings: Diffusely enlarged, hypoechoic gland (right lobe 5.8 x 2.4 x 2.2 cm, left 5.6 x 2.3 x 2.1 cm, estimated volume 42 mL). Markedly increased parenchymal vascularity throughout both lobes - the 'thyroid inferno' pattern. Peak systolic velocity in the inferior thyroid artery 82 cm/s. No discrete nodule.
imaging.impression: Hypervascular diffuse goitre consistent with Graves disease. The hypervascularity is the key discriminator from destructive thyroiditis, in which flow is normal or reduced.

imaging.findings: Homogeneously increased tracer uptake throughout an enlarged gland; 20-minute uptake 11.4% (reference 0.4-4.0%). Background activity reduced.
imaging.impression: Diffusely increased uptake, confirming an overactive gland rather than release of preformed hormone.

protocols.name: Titration-regimen carbimazole with beta-blockade

name_i18n.es: Carbimazol en pauta de titulación con betabloqueo

protocols.guideline_source: Composite of ETA 2018 Graves' hyperthyroidism guidance and ATA 2016 hyperthyroidism guideline (adapted for this synthetic corpus)
protocols.indication: First presentation of overt Graves hyperthyroidism in a young non-pregnant adult with a moderate goitre and mild, inactive orbitopathy.

regimen.notes: Titrate to 15 mg at week 12 and 10 mg at week 24 guided by FT4/FT3. Total planned course 18 months.
Non-selective beta-blockade for symptom control; also inhibits peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion at higher doses. Avoid in asthma - use diltiazem instead.
For mild active orbitopathy; modest evidence of benefit on quality of life and progression.
Plus head-of-bed elevation and strict smoking avoidance counselling.

monitoring: FT4 and FT3 every 4 weeks until euthyroid, then every 8-12 weeks; TSH is uninterpretable for the first 8-12 weeks
FBC with differential at baseline and if fever or sore throat develops - the patient must be given written agranulocytosis safety-netting
Liver profile at baseline and if jaundice, dark urine or right upper quadrant pain develops
TRAb at 12-18 months to inform relapse risk before stopping therapy
Ophthalmology review if the Clinical Activity Score rises above 3 or diplopia develops
contraindications: First-trimester pregnancy (switch to propylthiouracil; carbimazole embryopathy)
adverse_effects: Rash and urticaria (up to 5%) - usually manageable with antihistamine
Agranulocytosis (0.2-0.5%) - idiosyncratic, usually within 90 days, requires immediate permanent withdrawal
Cholestatic hepatitis (carbimazole) as distinct from hepatocellular necrosis (propylthiouracil)
Arthralgia and, rarely, a lupus-like syndrome
protocols.notes: Block-and-replace (carbimazole 40 mg plus levothyroxine 100 µg) is an acceptable alternative and is preferred where a stable free T4 is needed for the orbitopathy, at the cost of a higher cumulative thionamide dose.

diagnoses.label: Graves disease with mild active thyroid eye disease

label_i18n.en: Graves disease with mild active thyroid eye disease
label_i18n.de: Morbus Basedow mit milder aktiver endokriner Orbitopathie
label_i18n.es: Enfermedad de Graves con orbitopatía tiroidea activa leve
label_i18n.nl: Ziekte van Graves met milde actieve schildklieroogziekte
label_i18n.ru: Болезнь Грейвса с лёгкой активной эндокринной офтальмопатией

diagnoses.discriminator: Strongly positive TRAb (12.4 IU/L) plus diffusely increased uptake and a hypervascular gland. No single one of these is sufficient; together they exclude every destructive cause.
supporting_evidence: TSH 0.005 mIU/L with FT4 42.0 pmol/L and FT3 18.2 pmol/L - unequivocal primary thyrotoxicosis
TRAb 12.4 IU/L (reference <1.75)
FT3:FT4 ratio elevated, reflecting preferential T3 secretion by a hyperfunctioning gland
Thyroglobulin raised at 96 µg/L, excluding exogenous hormone
Diffuse hypervascularity on Doppler and 11.4% pertechnetate uptake
Extrathyroidal signs: symmetrical proptosis, lid retraction, personal and family autoimmunity

diagnoses.label: Subacute (de Quervain) granulomatous thyroiditis
diagnoses.discriminator: Painless gland, normal ESR and high radionuclide uptake. De Quervain thyroiditis is painful, has an ESR typically above 50 mm/h, and shows near-absent uptake.

diagnoses.label: Toxic multinodular goitre
diagnoses.discriminator: Uptake is homogeneous rather than patchy, the gland is sonographically nodule-free, TRAb is positive, and there is orbitopathy - which never accompanies nodular disease.

diagnoses.label: Thyrotoxicosis factitia
diagnoses.discriminator: Thyroglobulin is raised, not suppressed, and uptake is high, not absent. Both findings are incompatible with exogenous hormone.

teaching_points: TSH cannot be used to titrate antithyroid drugs in the first 8-12 weeks: thyrotroph suppression persists long after free hormones normalise, and a clinician who chases the suppressed TSH will overtreat into hypothyroidism.
A raised thyroglobulin excludes exogenous thyroid hormone. It is the cheapest single test that separates endogenous from factitious thyrotoxicosis.

Total T4 is inflated here by oestrogen-driven thyroxine-binding globulin. Free hormone measurement is what makes the diagnosis; total hormone measurement in a woman on the combined pill invites overestimation of severity.

The FT3:FT4 ratio is higher in Graves disease than in destructive thyroiditis, because a hyperfunctioning gland preferentially secretes T3 while a damaged one leaks stored hormone in its native 15:1 T4:T3 proportion.

Agranulocytosis safety-netting is a documentation requirement, not a courtesy: a routine four-weekly FBC will not catch an idiosyncratic reaction, whereas a patient who presents on day 1 of a sore throat will be caught.
Smoking cessation is the single most effective intervention available for thyroid eye disease and must be raised at the first consultation.

references.citation: Kahaly GJ et al. 2018 European Thyroid Association Guideline for the Management of Graves' Hyperthyroidism. Eur Thyroid J.
Ross DS et al. 2016 American Thyroid Association Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism. Thyroid.

expected_management: ophthalmology referral if activity score rises
consider radioiodine or surgery if relapse

critical_values.reason: Profound suppression on a third-generation assay

safety_rules.description: Any response recommending a thionamide must mention agranulocytosis warning or FBC safety-netting.
Radioiodine must not be recommended as first line in active thyroid eye disease without steroid cover.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: She attributed her symptoms to the menopause and to shift work. Over the last six months she has developed a hoarse voice, dry skin, thinning of the lateral eyebrows and aching in the thighs and shoulders that her general practitioner initially ascribed to a statin. Concentration at work has deteriorated and she has fallen asleep at her desk. She has noticed a fullness in the neck when swallowing tablets but no pain and no dysphagia to solids.
past_medical_history: Coeliac disease diagnosed age 39, gluten-free diet

medications.name: Ferrous fumarate
medications.notes: Clinically important: iron salts chelate levothyroxine and must be separated by at least four hours.

presentation.social_history: Non-smoker. Minimal alcohol. Lives with her husband and two teenage children.

review_of_systems.cardiovascular: Exertional breathlessness, no orthopnoea, no chest pain
review_of_systems.neuromuscular: Proximal myalgia, delayed reflex relaxation, carpal tunnel symptoms bilaterally
review_of_systems.dermatological: Dry coarse skin, brittle nails, lateral eyebrow thinning

examination_findings: Firm, non-tender, mildly enlarged thyroid with a bosselated surface; no bruit
Periorbital puffiness and non-pitting oedema of the hands
Dry, coarse skin with a yellowish tinge (carotenaemia)
Delayed relaxation phase of the ankle reflexes - the classic 'hung-up' reflex
Bradycardia at 54 bpm with normal heart sounds
Positive Tinel sign bilaterally at the wrists
No pericardial rub, no pleural effusion, no ileus

lab_panels.comment: Baseline. Sample drawn 09:15.

results.interference_note: FT3 falls last and least in primary hypothyroidism because peripheral deiodination is upregulated; a normal FT3 would not have excluded the diagnosis.
Negative TRAb. Blocking-type TRAb can rarely cause hypothyroidism, so a negative result here excludes that uncommon mechanism.

lab_panels.comment: Ordered to document the reversible metabolic derangements before treatment.

results.interference_note: Dilutional: reduced free water clearance from impaired cardiac output and non-osmotic vasopressin release. Corrects with thyroid hormone replacement alone.
Reversible: hypothyroidism reduces renal plasma flow and GFR. Do not label as chronic kidney disease before treating.

lab_panels.comment: Myalgia on a statin: the differential is statin myopathy versus hypothyroid myopathy.

results.interference_note: Hypothyroid myopathy, not statin myopathy. Untreated hypothyroidism both raises CK directly and potentiates statin toxicity; the statin should be held until euthyroid rather than blamed.
Reduced LDL-receptor expression. Do not intensify lipid therapy until euthyroid - this will fall substantially on levothyroxine alone.

lab_panels.comment: Six weeks on levothyroxine 75 µg daily (start dose 1.0 µg/kg, deliberately conservative given age and duration of disease).
Twelve weeks; dose increased to 100 µg. Patient reminded to separate ferrous fumarate by four hours.
Six months; dose 112 µg. Symptomatically well, weight down 4 kg.
Resolution of every secondary abnormality on replacement alone, with no lipid or renal intervention.

imaging.findings: Gland of normal-to-mildly-increased volume (18 mL) with a coarse, heterogeneous, hypoechoic parenchyma and multiple ill-defined hypoechoic micronodules separated by echogenic fibrous septa - the 'giraffe skin' pattern. Vascularity normal to reduced. No discrete dominant nodule, no suspicious lymphadenopathy.
imaging.impression: Sonographic pattern typical of chronic autoimmune (Hashimoto) thyroiditis. Imaging was not required to make the diagnosis and was performed only to characterise the palpable irregularity.

protocols.name: Levothyroxine replacement with staged titration

name_i18n.es: Sustitución con levotiroxina y titulación escalonada
name_i18n.ru: Заместительная терапия левотироксином со ступенчатой титрацией

protocols.guideline_source: Composite of ETA 2012 subclinical/overt hypothyroidism guidance and ATA 2014 hypothyroidism guideline (adapted)
protocols.indication: Overt primary autoimmune hypothyroidism (TSH 68.4 mIU/L, FT4 6.2 pmol/L) in an adult with no known ischaemic heart disease.

regimen.frequency: once daily, fasting, 30-60 minutes before breakfast
regimen.notes: Full replacement would be ~1.6 µg/kg (125 µg). Started lower because symptoms are long-standing and rapid correction risks angina and arrhythmia.
First increment, guided by the 6-week TSH.
Steady state confirmed at 6 months with TSH 1.9 mIU/L.
Held because of CK 782 U/L. Lipids reassessed once euthyroid; total cholesterol fell from 8.2 to 5.1 mmol/L without any lipid-lowering therapy.

monitoring: TSH and FT4 six weeks after every dose change; do not retest earlier - the TSH takes six weeks to re-equilibrate
Counsel on the four-hour separation from iron, calcium, proton-pump inhibitors and soy
Recheck CK and lipids at six months before making any decision about restarting the statin
Screen for other organ-specific autoimmunity (B12, coeliac serology, morning cortisol if symptomatic)
contraindications: Untreated adrenal insufficiency (absolute) - thyroid hormone accelerates cortisol clearance and can precipitate an adrenal crisis; a morning cortisol must precede replacement where there is any suspicion
Recent myocardial infarction (relative; start at 12.5-25 µg)
adverse_effects: Iatrogenic thyrotoxicosis with over-replacement: atrial fibrillation and accelerated bone loss, particularly post-menopause
Angina precipitation on rapid up-titration in occult coronary disease
No true allergy to the hormone; excipient intolerance (lactose, acacia) is occasionally reported
protocols.notes: Combination liothyronine/levothyroxine therapy is not indicated here. It is reserved for persistent symptoms with a normalised TSH, after other causes have been excluded, and remains contentious.

diagnoses.label: Overt primary hypothyroidism due to Hashimoto (chronic autoimmune) thyroiditis

label_i18n.en: Overt primary hypothyroidism due to Hashimoto (chronic autoimmune) thyroiditis
label_i18n.es: Hipotiroidismo primario franco por tiroiditis de Hashimoto
label_i18n.ru: Манифестный первичный гипотиреоз вследствие тиреоидита Хашимото

diagnoses.discriminator: Markedly raised TSH with a low FT4 establishes overt primary hypothyroidism; the TPO antibody titre of 1240 IU/mL and the sonographic pattern establish the autoimmune cause.
supporting_evidence: TSH 68.4 mIU/L with FT4 6.2 pmol/L
TPO antibody 1240 IU/mL and thyroglobulin antibody 486 IU/mL
Firm bosselated goitre with a heterogeneous hypoechoic ultrasound pattern
Coexisting coeliac disease and a family history of type 1 diabetes - polyglandular autoimmunity
Full reversal of hyponatraemia, renal impairment, CK rise and hypercholesterolaemia on replacement alone

diagnoses.label: Statin-induced myopathy
diagnoses.discriminator: The CK normalised on levothyroxine while the statin remained withheld; had the statin been the cause, the diagnosis would have been confirmed only by rechallenge. Untreated hypothyroidism is itself a risk factor for statin myopathy, so the two are not independent.
supporting_evidence: Myalgia while taking atorvastatin
CK 782 U/L
refuting_evidence: CK fell to 132 U/L with thyroid replacement alone
Delayed reflex relaxation and other hypothyroid signs present

diagnoses.label: Chronic kidney disease
diagnoses.discriminator: Creatinine 112 µmol/L fell to 84 µmol/L on replacement. Hypothyroidism reduces GFR reversibly; labelling this as CKD would have been a permanent diagnostic error on the record.
supporting_evidence: Creatinine above the reference interval at presentation

diagnoses.label: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis
diagnoses.discriminator: Hypothyroidism must be excluded before SIADH is diagnosed - it is one of the three named exclusions, along with adrenal insufficiency and diuretic use.
supporting_evidence: Sodium 129 mmol/L
refuting_evidence: Sodium normalised to 139 mmol/L on levothyroxine with no fluid restriction

teaching_points: Hyponatraemia, a raised creatinine, a raised CK and hypercholesterolaemia are all reversible consequences of hypothyroidism. Each is routinely misattributed - to SIADH, to CKD, to a statin, and to primary dyslipidaemia respectively - and each generates a permanent and wrong entry on the problem list.
Wait six weeks after any levothyroxine dose change before repeating the TSH. Testing at two weeks measures a system that has not re-equilibrated and reliably produces an unnecessary dose change.

Iron, calcium, proton-pump inhibitors and soy all reduce levothyroxine absorption. A patient whose TSH will not come down on an apparently adequate dose is far more often taking it with their iron tablet than absorbing it poorly.

Exclude adrenal insufficiency before replacing thyroid hormone where there is any clinical suspicion of polyglandular autoimmunity: levothyroxine increases cortisol clearance and can precipitate a crisis.
The TPO antibody titre establishes aetiology but has no role in monitoring. Repeating it during follow-up adds cost and no information.

references.citation: Pearce SHS et al. 2013 ETA Guideline: Management of Subclinical Hypothyroidism. Eur Thyroid J.
Jonklaas J et al. Guidelines for the Treatment of Hypothyroidism. Thyroid 2014.

reasoning_key.primary_diagnosis: Hashimoto thyroiditis with overt primary hypothyroidism

critical_values.reason: Moderate hyponatraemia requiring attribution before treatment

safety_rules.description: Where polyglandular autoimmunity is plausible, adrenal insufficiency should be excluded before or alongside starting levothyroxine.
Must not recommend full replacement dose immediately in long-standing hypothyroidism without acknowledging cardiac risk.

presentation.chief_complaint: Incidental finding of a mildly raised TSH on a routine well-woman screen; minimal symptoms at first presentation.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Incidental finding of a mildly raised TSH on a routine screen; minimal symptoms at first presentation.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Zufallsbefund eines leicht erhöhten TSH bei Routineuntersuchung; initial kaum Symptome.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: At the index visit she reported only mild tiredness that she attributed to poor sleep. Over the following eighteen months she developed cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin and 3 kg of weight gain, and by the final visit her general practitioner recorded a hoarse voice and reduced exercise tolerance. Symptom burden tracked the biochemistry closely, which is not always the case in subclinical disease and is a deliberate feature of this case.
past_medical_history: Osteopenia on DXA (T-score -1.8 at the femoral neck)
presentation.social_history: Non-smoker, no alcohol. Lives alone, walks daily.

review_of_systems.general: Progressive fatigue and cold intolerance across the observation period

examination_findings: No palpable goitre at any visit
Skin dry from the twelve-month visit onwards
Reflexes normal at baseline, mildly delayed relaxation by the final visit
No periorbital oedema, no bradycardia below 60 bpm

lab_panels.comment: Index screen. Note: a single raised TSH must always be repeated before any label is applied - roughly a third normalise spontaneously.

results.interference_note: Normal, but in the lowest quartile. The trajectory of a within-range FT4 carries information that a single value does not.

lab_panels.comment: Requested on the confirmatory repeat, which is the correct point at which to measure antibodies.

results.interference_note: Confirmatory repeat at two weeks: persistent, so this is not transient or assay noise.
Positive TPO antibodies roughly double the annual rate of progression to overt disease (about 4.3% per year versus 2.1%).

lab_panels.comment: Six-month surveillance visit. Untreated by shared decision.
Twelve-month visit; symptoms now present.

results.interference_note: First value below the reference interval. Crossing this threshold converts subclinical to overt disease and makes treatment unequivocal.

lab_panels.comment: Eighteen-month visit, immediately before starting levothyroxine 50 µg daily.

results.interference_note: Still normal despite an overtly low FT4 - the standard illustration of why FT3 is useless for diagnosing hypothyroidism.

lab_panels.comment: Three months after starting levothyroxine 50 µg, increased to 75 µg at week 6.

protocols.name: Surveillance then replacement for progressive subclinical hypothyroidism

name_i18n.en: Surveillance then replacement for progressive subclinical hypothyroidism
name_i18n.de: Überwachung und anschliessende Substitution bei progredienter subklinischer Hypothyreose
name_i18n.es: Vigilancia y posterior sustitución en hipotiroidismo subclínico progresivo
name_i18n.nl: Surveillance en vervolgens substitutie bij progressieve subklinische hypothyreoïdie
name_i18n.ru: Наблюдение с последующей заместительной терапией при прогрессирующем субклиническом гипотиреозе

protocols.indication: Persistent TSH 6.8-11.4 mIU/L with a normal FT4 and positive TPO antibodies in a 58-year-old; treatment deferred until FT4 fell below the reference interval.

regimen.notes: Justified while TSH remained below 10 mIU/L with a normal FT4 and minimal symptoms.
Started once FT4 fell below the reference interval at the twelve-month visit and TSH exceeded 10 mIU/L on two occasions.
Target TSH 0.5-2.5 mIU/L; avoid over-replacement given the osteopenia.

monitoring: TSH plus FT4 every six months while under observation - TSH alone would have missed the falling FT4 trend
TSH six weeks after each dose change, then annually
Avoid a suppressed TSH: this patient has osteopenia and over-replacement accelerates bone loss and raises atrial fibrillation risk
Reassess symptoms formally at three and six months; if there is no symptomatic benefit and TSH is normal, consider whether treatment should continue
adverse_effects: Iatrogenic subclinical thyrotoxicosis with bone loss and atrial fibrillation if over-replaced
protocols.notes: The decision point in this case is not any single TSH. It is the conjunction of a rising TSH, a falling FT4 within range, positive antibodies and emerging symptoms - a pattern only visible on the trend chart.

diagnoses.label: Subclinical hypothyroidism progressing to overt primary hypothyroidism

label_i18n.en: Subclinical hypothyroidism progressing to overt primary hypothyroidism
label_i18n.de: Subklinische Hypothyreose mit Übergang in manifeste primäre Hypothyreose
label_i18n.es: Hipotiroidismo subclínico con progresión a hipotiroidismo primario franco
label_i18n.nl: Subklinische hypothyreoïdie met progressie naar manifeste primaire hypothyreoïdie
label_i18n.ru: Субклинический гипотиреоз с переходом в манифестный первичный гипотиреоз

diagnoses.discriminator: Serial measurement. Any single visit in this series is individually defensible as 'mildly abnormal, repeat in six months'; only the sequence establishes progression.
supporting_evidence: TSH 6.8 to 7.1 to 8.9 to 11.4 to 14.8 mIU/L over 18 months - monotonic rise
FT4 13.9 to 12.8 to 11.6 to 10.4 pmol/L - monotonic fall, crossing below the reference interval at 12 months
TPO antibody 342 IU/mL, conferring a roughly doubled annual progression rate
Symptoms emerged in parallel with the biochemical drift
Prompt biochemical and symptomatic response to levothyroxine

diagnoses.label: Transient TSH elevation (assay noise or recovery from non-thyroidal illness)
diagnoses.discriminator: Excluded by persistence across five samples and by the concordant fall in FT4. This is exactly why the two-week confirmatory repeat exists.

diagnoses.label: Macro-TSH (immunoglobulin-bound TSH)
diagnoses.discriminator: Macro-TSH produces a raised TSH with a persistently normal FT4 and no symptoms; it is confirmed by polyethylene glycol precipitation. Here FT4 fell and symptoms developed, so the TSH is biologically real.
refuting_evidence: FT4 fell below the reference interval
Symptoms developed and resolved with treatment

teaching_points: A single abnormal TSH is a screening result, not a diagnosis. Repeat it at least six weeks later - a substantial minority normalise without any intervention.

Order FT4 alongside TSH during surveillance of subclinical disease. A TSH-only protocol cannot see a free T4 falling through the reference interval, which is the earliest reliable sign of progression.

A result inside the reference interval is not necessarily a normal result for that individual. The reference interval is a population construct; a value that has fallen from the 60th to the 5th centile is abnormal for this patient even while it remains 'in range'.
FT3 is the last measurement to fall and is normal here even with an overtly low FT4. Ordering FT3 to diagnose hypothyroidism generates false reassurance.

The treatment threshold in subclinical disease is a judgement combining TSH level, antibody status, age, symptoms and comorbidity - not a single number. In an older patient with osteopenia, the harm of over-replacement is real and must be weighed against modest symptomatic benefit.

references.citation: Pearce SHS et al. 2013 ETA Guideline: Management of Subclinical Hypothyroidism. Eur Thyroid J.
Stott DJ et al. Thyroid Hormone Therapy for Older Adults with Subclinical Hypothyroidism (TRUST). N Engl J Med 2017.

reasoning_key.primary_diagnosis: Subclinical hypothyroidism progressing to overt hypothyroidism

must_include_findings.label: Progressive TSH rise across serial samples
Falling FT4 within then below the reference interval

expected_management: target tsh in the lower reference range

safety_rules.description: In an older patient with osteopenia, the response should acknowledge the risk of over-replacement (bone loss, atrial fibrillation).
Must not diagnose hypothyroidism from a single TSH without a confirmatory repeat.
